summary: Auth.js v5 Node-runtime instance. Credentials provider with bcrypt compare, JWT strategy (maxAge 8h). authorize() checks isActive BEFORE the password compare so a deactivated account is indistinguishable by timing, and captures tokenVersion at mint time. The session callback deliberately does NOT copy tokenVersion — anything on Session is served by GET /api/auth/session.
Edge-safe Auth.js base config: no adapter, no providers, no Node imports. Exposes pages.signIn=/login and an authorized callback. Consumed by middleware for a coarse session check.

THE authorization choke point, 32 importers. Three gates: getCurrentUser (no redirect), requireActiveUser (session-only pages), requireRole (roles + Server Actions). The DATABASE is authoritative — the JWT supplies only an id. Strictly Node-runtime.

getCurrentUser — decodes the cookie for an id, then reads the live User row for role/isActive/mustChangePassword/tokenVersion. Refuses a tokenVersion mismatch AND a token carrying no claim at all (not defaulted to 0). FAILS CLOSED: a throwing lookup is deliberately uncaught, so an outage or unapplied migration surfaces as an error, never as a silent logout.

readSessionToken — reads the RAW JWT rather than calling auth(), so the revocation claim never reaches the wire. Tries __Secure-authjs.session-token then authjs.session-token; the cookie name is the encryption salt, so the two cannot be confused. Request-scoped via cache().

requireActiveUser — the gate for pages with no role rule. Exists SEPARATELY from the (dashboard) layout because Next does not re-render a shared layout on soft navigation, so a user deactivated mid-session would keep browsing. 14 pages use it.

Permission matrix, 30 importers. Permission union, ROLE_PERMISSIONS per Role, can(role, permission), and named role-group constants used by Server Actions instead of inline literals. ADMIN_MANAGE_ROLES gates the whole user lifecycle.
loginAction (useActionState signature) and logoutAction. Returns {error} rather than throwing.
Centered-card layout for the (auth) group. Performs NO session check — load-bearing, because /change-password lives here and must not redirect-loop through the dashboard gate.

changePassword — resolves its caller with getCurrentUser() (NOT requireRole) so it can never bounce itself into a redirect loop. Clears mustChangePassword and increments tokenVersion, revoking every other live session.

Module augmentation adding id and role to Session.user and id/role/tokenVersion to the JWT. tokenVersion is deliberately absent from the Session augmentation so it cannot be re-added by accident — see auth-001.

Edge middleware: IP-keyed fixed-window rate limiter wrapping NextAuth's coarse session check. Matcher WIDENED to stop excluding /login. NOTE: middleware.ts is deprecated in Next.js 16 in favour of proxy.ts (Node runtime).

getClientIp() reads x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip and returns string | null. TRUST BOUNDARY: with no reverse proxy in front (the shipped compose topology) this value is attacker-controlled on every request. Returns null rather than a shared 'unknown' key — the caller skips rate limiting entirely, because a shared bucket produced a measured DoS.
Rate-limit decision. POST /login is treated as a credential attempt and gets the stricter AUTH_RATE_LIMIT alongside /api/auth/*; a null IP skips rate limiting.
Prisma 7 client singleton using @prisma/adapter-pg, cached on globalThis in dev. Highest fan-in module in the codebase (33 importers).

17 models and enums. User now carries isActive, mustChangePassword and tokenVersion. Auth.js scaffolding (Account/Session/VerificationToken) is unused under the JWT strategy. CRM, service desk, billing and QuickBooksConnection as before.

TimeEntry. ticket relation is onDelete: Cascade — deleting a Ticket destroys its time entries. invoiceLineItem is onDelete: SetNull, so the billed line item survives. This asymmetry is a billing-integrity hazard for any ticket-delete path.

User.tokenVersion — the token-generation counter. Every JWT carries the value current when minted; getCurrentUser() refuses a mismatch. Incrementing revokes every session issued before it, which is what makes a password reset actually terminate a stolen session.

10 timestamped migrations: init, add_crm_core, add_ticketing, add_time_tracking_billing, fix_time_entry_invoice_line_item_not_unique, add_reporting_indexes, add_reporting_indexes_followup, add_defense_in_depth_indexes, add_user_activation_fields, add_user_token_version.

Upsert loop over the five roles with bcrypt-hashed passwords. Throws under NODE_ENV=production unless ALLOW_SEED_IN_PRODUCTION=true. E2E fixtures depend on these accounts. No longer the only user-creation path — see adm-001 and adm-004.

The user-lifecycle Server Actions: createUser, resetUserPassword, updateUserRole, deactivateUser, reactivateUser. All gated by requireRole(ADMIN_MANAGE_ROLES). Self-target and last-active-admin guard rails are enforced here, not by the role constant.

Temporary-password generation. 32-symbol alphabet excluding 0/O/1/I/l; length 32 is load-bearing because 256 % 32 == 0, so `byte % 32` has no modulo bias. A module-load assertion throws if a future edit breaks that divisibility. 20 symbols = 100 bits.

ADMIN_INVARIANT_LOCK_KEY (7030303) — a transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock serializing the last-active-admin invariant. EVERY code path that could reduce the number of active admins MUST take this same key, or it is not serialized against the others.

Bootstrap logic for creating or resetting the first admin OUTSIDE the running app. Pure-ish helpers (resolveDatabaseUrl, normalizeBootstrapEmail, validateBootstrapPassword, explainPrismaFailure) plus findBootstrapAccount / createBootstrapAdmin / resetBootstrapAdminPassword. Zero importers in src/ — consumed by scripts/create-admin.ts and its spec.
The `npm run bootstrap:admin` CLI. Interactive create/reset of an admin account; delegates all logic to src/lib/bootstrap-admin.ts. The recovery path when no admin can log in.
User administration table. Gates with requireRole(ADMIN_MANAGE_ROLES) — the authoritative convention. Its own header contrasts itself with /admin/quickbooks, which predates it.
Per-row admin controls — reset password, change role, deactivate/reactivate — with alert-dialog confirmations. The largest component in the codebase.
Admin form for creating a user; surfaces the generated temporary password once.
zod schemas for the user lifecycle, including MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH (12) that the temp-password generator must also clear.
Ticket Server Actions: createTicket, updateTicket, updateTicketStatus, assignTicket, deleteTicket. Gated by TICKET_MANAGE_ROLES / TICKET_ASSIGN_ROLES.

deleteTicket — ownership-scoped. Has ZERO call sites in src/. Its docstring names only the TicketComment cascade and omits the TimeEntry cascade, so calling it silently destroys billing records. See db-003.
Timer Server Actions: startTimer (per-user already-running guard), stopTimer, updateTimeEntry, deleteTimeEntry. Gated by TIME_ENTRY_MANAGE_ROLES.
generateInvoice (date range per company, applies contract billing rules), finalizeInvoice, pushInvoiceToQbo. Gated by INVOICE_MANAGE_ROLES.
QBO invoice line construction hardcodes ItemRef: { value: "1" } — every pushed line references QuickBooks item id 1. Accepted debt since Phase 4; needs a real item mapping.
createCompany, updateCompany, deleteCompany. Gated by CRM_MANAGE_ROLES. The reference example of the Server Action shape.
createSite, updateSite, deleteSite — sites belong to a company.
createContact, updateContact, deleteContact.
createContract, updateContract, deleteContract. Contracts carry billing type and SLA targets consumed by sla.ts and billing.ts.
createAsset, updateAsset, deleteAsset — devices tied to a company and optionally a site.
addComment — appends a TicketComment. Also the mechanism the email poller and SLA sweep use to record breach flags.
disconnectQbo and setCompanyQboCustomerId. Gated by QBO_MANAGE_ROLES (admin only).
Pure billing rules, no Prisma. computeBlockHourCharge, computeFlatFeeCharge, computeHourlyBreakfixCharge, and the computeContractCharges dispatcher over BillingType.
Pure SLA logic. computeSlaDeadlines derives response/resolution deadlines from contract targets; getSlaStatus returns no_sla | on_track | approaching | breached | met.
computeElapsedMinutes and formatDuration — pure helpers shared by TimerControl and the time entry list.

All three reports plus date-range helpers. getTechnicianUtilization, getSlaCompliance, getClientProfitability, parseDateRangeBoundaries, isValidDateString, getCurrentMonthRange. The only module with direct unit coverage.
AES-256-GCM encrypt/decrypt over TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Added in Phase 6 to stop QuickBooks OAuth tokens being written to the database in plaintext.

QuickBooks Online OAuth and client. exchangeCodeForTokens, refreshAccessToken, getValidQboClient (refresh-on-expiry), buildAuthorizeUrl. Tokens round-trip through crypto.ts. Endpoint URLs were never verified against Intuit's live docs.
isNextRedirectError — required whenever redirect() is called inside a try/catch, because Next signals redirects by throwing. 12 importers.
cn() — clsx + tailwind-merge class combiner used by every shadcn component. 13 importers.
9 zod schemas: company, site, contact, contract, asset, ticket, time-entry, invoice, user. Each exports a schema plus an inferred Input type. Server Actions parse here rather than inline.
contractSchema is a zod discriminatedUnion over billingType — the most structurally interesting validator in the codebase. Changing BillingType requires editing this union.

Authenticated shell. Calls the session gate and redirects; renders role-aware AppSidebar and UserMenu. NOTE: a shared layout does NOT re-render on soft navigation — that is why requireActiveUser() also runs in each leaf page (auth-006).
Dashboard home with role-aware summary content.
Ticket detail — comments, assignment control, timer control, time entry list, SLA badge. The natural home for a delete control, which still does not exist.
Kanban board page — the primary dispatch surface.
Company detail with tabbed sub-views (sites, contacts, contracts, assets), each an async Server Component.

QBO connection status, connect/disconnect, company->QBO customer mapping. Gates by open-coding getCurrentUser() + can(role,'qbo:manage') + manual redirects — it PREDATES the requireRole convention. Use it as a LAYOUT model only, never as a gating model.
Three report pages — utilization, sla, profitability — each reading src/lib/reporting.ts and gated by REPORT_VIEW_ALL_ROLES for the cross-user views.
Invoice list and detail. Detail hosts InvoiceLineTable and PushToQboButton.

Re-exports NextAuth GET/POST handlers. NOTE: GET /api/auth/session is exempt from the middleware session gate and never consults getCurrentUser(), so it answers for tokens getCurrentUser() refuses — which is why tokenVersion is kept off Session.
Starts the QBO OAuth flow; sets the qbo_oauth_state cookie and redirects to Intuit.
QBO OAuth callback — validates state, exchanges the code, encrypts tokens via crypto.ts before persisting QuickBooksConnection.
Shared loading and error boundaries covering the dashboard routes (error.tsx alongside).
Role-aware navigation. Now a real Admin SECTION with two gated destinations: /admin/quickbooks (qbo:manage) and /admin/users (admin:manage_users). The previous dead else-branch is gone.
@dnd-kit drag-and-drop board; drops call updateTicketStatus. Uses snap-x/lg:snap-none for the responsive breakpoint.
Start/stop timer widget driving startTimer and stopTimer.
Renders SLA status via theme tokens. on_track and met share styling and are distinguished by label text.
Ticket create/edit form plus the separate AssignmentControl, which calls assignTicket directly without navigation.
CRM forms and tabs. The *-tab.tsx files are async Server Components; the *-form.tsx files are client forms. Shared CrmTabProps in tab-types.ts.
GenerateInvoiceForm, InvoiceLineTable, InvoiceStatusBadge, PushToQboButton.
DateRangeFilter, CompanyContractFilter, UtilizationTable, ProfitabilityTable, SlaComplianceSummary.
13 shadcn/ui primitives over radix-ui, including alert-dialog (added for admin confirmations). Generated — avoid hand-editing.

Standalone worker run as its own Compose service. Microsoft Graph mailbox poll creating tickets from email, plus checkSlaBreaches() sweep. requireEnv() fails fast on AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, MAILBOX_ADDRESS.
SLA_BREACH_MARKER = '[SLA BREACH]' — a greppable prefix on breach comments used as the re-notification guard. Changing the string orphans every already-flagged breach.

THREE projects, and the split is load-bearing. lifecycle = the blocking gate; last-active-admin depends on lifecycle and is fullyParallel:false because its precondition is that the seeded admin is the only active admin; advisory = the three never-run pre-Phase-7 specs, which block nothing. reuseExistingServer:false ALWAYS, so a run can never grade a stale container.
Resolves WHICH server is graded (E2E_BASE_URL / E2E_PORT / E2E_SERVER_IS_EXTERNAL). Documents the stale-container failure this replaced and the three defences against it.
Build-identity check against the server under test — runs even when the server is caller-managed. Paired with global-teardown.ts.
The Phase 7 blocking gate — the largest spec in the repo. Covers create/reset/re-role/deactivate/reactivate end to end.

Guard-rail spec for the last-active-admin invariant. CANNOT be correct while another spec holds a second active admin open — hence its own project, dependencies:[lifecycle] and fullyParallel:false. See adm-003.
Tests this suite's own two silent-wrong-answer helpers, and so belongs to the run whose conclusions they decide. Part of the lifecycle project deliberately.
Shared database access for the specs and both global hooks.
Shared Playwright fixtures — loginAs(role) and ROLE_CREDENTIALS for the seeded roles. Every spec depends on the seeded accounts.
Ticket lifecycle E2E, in the advisory project — never run against a browser. Holds two test.fixme cases for ownership-scoped delete, skipped because no delete UI exists to drive.
The only direct unit/regression coverage in the codebase, over reporting.ts date handling and aggregation.

Three services: app (publishes 3000:3000, NO reverse proxy — see mw-002), email-poller, db (postgres:16-alpine, publishes ${DB_PORT:-5432}). postgres:postgres credentials appear in all three service definitions.

Scripts include bootstrap:admin plus three e2e entry points: test:e2e (lifecycle + last-active-admin = the gate), test:e2e:advisory, test:e2e:all. Next 16.3.3, React 19.2.8, Prisma 7.10, next-auth 5 beta, zod 4, Tailwind 4.
Empty NextConfig. Relevant because the Next 16 middleware->proxy migration renames config flags (skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize -> skipProxyUrlNormalize); neither is set here.
